requirements.quote:
t:  The size of the authentication tag in bits.  For these ciphers, t
      is 128.
requirements.condition: When applying the AEAD usage analysis to the ciphers covered by this appendix
requirements.required_behavior: Set authentication-tag size t to 128 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another t value in these formulas.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured tag size and formula input can be compared directly with 128 bits.

requirements.quote:
n:  The size of the block function in bits.  For these ciphers, n is
      128.
requirements.condition: When applying the AEAD usage analysis to the ciphers covered by this appendix
requirements.required_behavior: Set block-function size n to 128 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another n value in these formulas.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured block size and formula input can be compared directly with 128 bits.

requirements.quote:
k:  The size of the key in bits.  This is 128 for AEAD_AES_128_GCM
      and AEAD_AES_128_CCM; 256 for AEAD_AES_256_GCM.
requirements.condition: When analyzing AEAD_AES_128_GCM
requirements.required_behavior: Set key-size parameter k to 128 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another k value for AEAD_AES_128_GCM.
requirements.why_checkable: The algorithm key size and formula parameter can be compared with 128 bits.

requirements.quote:
k:  The size of the key in bits.  This is 128 for AEAD_AES_128_GCM
      and AEAD_AES_128_CCM; 256 for AEAD_AES_256_GCM.
requirements.condition: When analyzing AEAD_AES_128_CCM
requirements.required_behavior: Set key-size parameter k to 128 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another k value for AEAD_AES_128_CCM.
requirements.why_checkable: The algorithm key size and formula parameter can be compared with 128 bits.

requirements.quote:
k:  The size of the key in bits.  This is 128 for AEAD_AES_128_GCM
      and AEAD_AES_128_CCM; 256 for AEAD_AES_256_GCM.
requirements.condition: When analyzing AEAD_AES_256_GCM
requirements.required_behavior: Set key-size parameter k to 256 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another k value for AEAD_AES_256_GCM.
requirements.why_checkable: The algorithm key size and formula parameter can be compared with 256 bits.

requirements.quote: l:  The number of blocks in each packet (see below).
requirements.condition: When evaluating the AEAD usage-limit formulas
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret l as the number of analyzed blocks in each packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret l as a byte count or packet count.
requirements.why_checkable: Formula implementations can be inspected to verify the unit and source of l.

requirements.quote:
q:  The number of genuine packets created and protected by endpoints.
      This value is the bound on the number of packets that can be
      protected before updating keys.
requirements.condition: When enforcing a confidentiality usage limit for one key generation
requirements.required_behavior: Count q as the number of genuine packets created and protected before keys are updated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reset or omit genuine protected packets from q without a key update.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet counter can be compared with the number of genuine protected packets emitted between key-update events.

requirements.quote:
v:  The number of forged packets that endpoints will accept.  This
      value is the bound on the number of forged packets that an
      endpoint can reject before updating keys.
requirements.condition: When enforcing an integrity usage limit for one key generation
requirements.required_behavior: Use v as the bound on forged-packet protection-removal attempts before updating keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reset or omit failed forged-packet attempts from the integrity-limit accounting without a key update.
requirements.why_checkable: Failed authentication attempts can be counted between key updates and compared with the implementation's v accounting.

requirements.quote: o:  The amount of offline ideal cipher queries made by an adversary.
requirements.condition: When evaluating the full GCM integrity-advantage formula
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret o as the adversary's number of offline ideal-cipher queries.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Substitute an endpoint packet count for o.
requirements.why_checkable: A formula implementation can be inspected to verify the semantic unit assigned to o.

requirements.quote:
This analysis is
   performed for packets of size up to 2^11 (l = 2^7)
requirements.condition: When using the smaller-packet-size AEAD analysis
requirements.required_behavior: Use a maximum packet size of 2^11 bytes and l = 2^7 blocks.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply that l value to packets larger than 2^11 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The enforced packet-size cap and l input can be compared with 2048 bytes and 128 blocks.

requirements.condition: When using the maximum-packet-size AEAD analysis
requirements.required_behavior: Use a maximum packet size of 2^16 bytes and l = 2^12 blocks.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the smaller l = 2^7 premise for an endpoint that permits packets up to 2^16 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The analysis inputs can be compared with 65536 bytes and 4096 blocks.

requirements.quote:
the 2^16 is the maximum possible size of
   a QUIC packet.
requirements.condition: When selecting the conservative packet-size premise for this AEAD analysis
requirements.required_behavior: Use 2^16 bytes as the maximum analyzed QUIC packet size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Base these bounds on a larger QUIC packet size without a new analysis.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet-size premise used by a limit calculator can be read and compared with 2^16 bytes.

requirements.quote:
Only endpoints that strictly limit packet size can
   use the larger confidentiality and integrity limits that are derived
   using the smaller packet size.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint applies confidentiality or integrity limits derived from the 2^11-byte packet-size analysis
requirements.required_behavior: Strictly enforce the corresponding smaller maximum packet size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the larger usage limits while accepting or sending packets above the assumed size bound.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-size enforcement can be stress-tested and compared with the size premise selected by the endpoint's usage-limit counters.

requirements.quote:
For AEAD_AES_128_GCM and AEAD_AES_256_GCM, the message length (l) is
   the length of the associated data in blocks plus the length of the
   plaintext in blocks.
requirements.condition: When computing l for AEAD_AES_128_GCM or AEAD_AES_256_GCM
requirements.required_behavior: Compute l as associated_data_blocks + plaintext_blocks.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exclude either associated-data or plaintext blocks from l.
requirements.why_checkable: For known associated-data and plaintext lengths, l can be recomputed and compared with the implementation's value.

requirements.quote:
For AEAD_AES_128_CCM, the total number of block cipher operations is
   the sum of the following: the length of the associated data in
   blocks, the length of the ciphertext in blocks, the length of the
   plaintext in blocks, plus 1.
requirements.condition: When computing the exact per-packet block-cipher operation count for AEAD_AES_128_CCM
requirements.required_behavior: Compute operations as associated_data_blocks + ciphertext_blocks + plaintext_blocks + 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit any listed term from the exact operation count.
requirements.why_checkable: Each encoded length can be converted to blocks and the summed operation count compared with the formula.

requirements.quote:
this is simplified to
   a value of twice the length of the packet in blocks (that is, "2l =
   2^8" for packets that are limited to 2^11 bytes
requirements.condition: When applying the simplified AEAD_AES_128_CCM analysis with packets limited to 2^11 bytes
requirements.required_behavior: Use the operation-count approximation 2l = 2^8.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the maximum-size 2l value for this strictly limited case.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected CCM analysis constant can be compared directly with 256 block operations.

requirements.quote:
or "2l = 2^13"
   otherwise).
requirements.condition: When applying the simplified AEAD_AES_128_CCM analysis without the 2^11-byte packet-size restriction
requirements.required_behavior: Use the operation-count approximation 2l = 2^13.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use 2l = 2^8 without strictly enforcing the smaller packet-size limit.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected CCM analysis constant can be compared directly with 8192 block operations.

requirements.quote:
The number of ciphertext blocks an attacker uses in forgery
      attempts is bounded by v * l
requirements.condition: When reproducing the GCM multi-user integrity analysis
requirements.required_behavior: Bound attacker forgery-attempt ciphertext blocks by v * l.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a forgery-block bound greater than v * l under this simplifying assumption.
requirements.why_checkable: Given v and l, an analysis implementation's forgery-block bound can be compared directly with their product.

requirements.quote:
for
   a single user that does not repeat nonces
requirements.condition: When applying the stated GCM confidentiality bound to one user under one key
requirements.required_behavior: Use a distinct nonce for every protected packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Repeat a nonce under the analyzed key.
requirements.why_checkable: Captured nonce inputs can be checked for duplicates within a key generation.

requirements.condition: When calculating the dominant GCM confidentiality distinguishing-advantage term
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate the term as 2 * (q * l)^2 / 2^n.
requirements.why_checkable: The expression can be evaluated for fixed q, l, and n and compared numerically with a limit calculator.

requirements.quote: For a target advantage of 2^-57
requirements.condition: When deriving the GCM confidentiality packet limit in this appendix
requirements.required_behavior: Use 2^-57 as the target maximum distinguishing advantage.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive the stated q limits from a weaker target advantage.
requirements.why_checkable: The threshold input to the derivation can be inspected and compared with 2^-57.

requirements.condition: When enforcing the derived GCM confidentiality bound
requirements.required_behavior: Keep q less than or equal to 2^35 / l.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect a packet that makes q exceed 2^35 / l without changing keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The protected-packet counter and l can be substituted into the exact inequality at runtime.

requirements.quote:
endpoints that do not send packets larger than 2^11 bytes
   cannot protect more than 2^28 packets in a single connection
requirements.condition: When a GCM endpoint sends no packet larger than 2^11 bytes in a connection
requirements.required_behavior: Protect at most 2^28 packets in that connection under the stated confidentiality target.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect more than 2^28 packets without applying a new usage regime or keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The maximum sent packet size and total protected-packet count can be measured for a connection and compared with 2^11 and 2^28.

requirements.quote:
The limit for endpoints that allow for the packet
   size to be as large as 2^16 is instead 2^23.
requirements.condition: When a GCM endpoint allows packet sizes up to 2^16 bytes
requirements.required_behavior: Limit protected packets to at most 2^23 under the stated confidentiality target.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect more than 2^23 packets without applying a new usage regime or keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured size class and protected-packet counter can be compared with the exact 2^23 limit.

requirements.condition: When calculating the full upper bound on GCM forgery advantage
requirements.why_checkable: A limit calculator can be evaluated at fixed n, v, o, k, and l and compared term-by-term with the stated expression.

requirements.quote: The goal is to limit this advantage to 2^-57.
requirements.condition: When deriving the GCM integrity attempt limits in this appendix
requirements.required_behavior: Use 2^-57 as the maximum target forgery advantage.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive the stated v limits from a weaker target advantage.
requirements.why_checkable: The integrity-threshold input to the derivation can be inspected and compared with 2^-57.

requirements.condition: When applying the AEAD_AES_128_GCM integrity approximation
requirements.required_behavior: Keep v less than or equal to 2^64 / l.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempt to remove protection from a packet that makes v exceed 2^64 / l without changing keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The failed protection-removal counter and l can be substituted into the exact inequality at runtime.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints that do not attempt to remove protection from packets
   larger than 2^11 bytes can attempt to remove protection from at most
   2^57 packets.
requirements.condition: When an AEAD_AES_128_GCM endpoint never attempts protection removal on packets larger than 2^11 bytes
requirements.required_behavior: Attempt protection removal on at most 2^57 packets before updating keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exceed 2^57 protection-removal attempts under the same keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet sizes and protection-removal attempts can be counted per key generation and compared with the exact limits.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints that do not restrict the size of processed
   packets can attempt to remove protection from at most 2^52 packets.
requirements.condition: When an AEAD_AES_128_GCM endpoint does not enforce the 2^11-byte processed-packet limit
requirements.required_behavior: Attempt protection removal on at most 2^52 packets before updating keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exceed 2^52 protection-removal attempts under the same keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's size policy and protection-removal attempt counter can be checked against the 2^52 bound.

requirements.condition: When applying the AEAD_AES_256_GCM integrity approximation
requirements.required_behavior: Keep v less than or equal to 2^192 / l.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a v value beyond the stated approximation without a different analysis.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected v and l can be substituted into the exact inequality used by a limit calculator.

requirements.quote:
this document recommends that the same limit be applied to
   both functions
requirements.condition: When enforcing GCM integrity limits for AEAD_AES_256_GCM
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the same protection-removal attempt limit used for AEAD_AES_128_GCM.
requirements.why_checkable: Configured counters for AES-128-GCM and AES-256-GCM can be compared for equal integrity thresholds under the same packet-size policy.

requirements.quote:
any AEAD that is used with QUIC requires
   limits on use that ensure that both confidentiality and integrity are
   preserved.
requirements.condition: When an AEAD algorithm is used with QUIC
requirements.required_behavior: Enforce a usage limit sufficient to preserve confidentiality.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the AEAD without any confidentiality usage bound.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected for a confidentiality counter and tested at its configured exhaustion boundary.

requirements.quote:
any AEAD that is used with QUIC requires
   limits on use that ensure that both confidentiality and integrity are
   preserved.
requirements.condition: When an AEAD algorithm is used with QUIC
requirements.required_behavior: Enforce a usage limit sufficient to preserve integrity.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the AEAD without any integrity-attempt usage bound.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected for an integrity-attempt counter and tested at its configured exhaustion boundary.

requirements.condition: When calculating the stated AEAD_AES_128_CCM confidentiality distinguishing-advantage bound
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate the bound as (2l * q)^2 / 2^n.
requirements.why_checkable: The expression can be evaluated for fixed l, q, and n and compared numerically with a CCM limit calculator.
